Driven on the real binary, processes on one database (throwaway probe, $TMPDIR/infra228/probes/r5/zz_tester_r5_test.go on the tester's volume): old configuration fixes legion-daemon:ACME for example-daemon (A); new fixes it for example-other (C). After C's first exchange on the new process (holder C, infinity) and an old process restarted mid-rollout: A exchanges on that old process -> 200, holder now A (infinity); C on the new process -> 200, holder C; A on the old process -> 200, holder A; then A, which the new configuration fixes nothing for, asks the name on the NEW process -> 200, because A holds it. Each process logged `took a session name the configuration fixes from its holder` twice. So a name leaves its holder a third way, the old entry's own exchange at a process of the old configuration after the re-point has already landed, and a principal the current configuration does not fix the name for is answered 200 for it, on new processes, until the new entry next exchanges. It settles once the last old-configuration process stops and the new entry exchanges again; it never locks the new entry out (C got 200 at every one of its exchanges). Everything else claimed holds (exercised). How to close it is the architect's call: the body describes this alternation and its bound (it lasts while any process of the old configuration serves, so a stalled rollout prolongs it), or the code orders configurations. No red test, since it is the body's claim that is false and the behaviour is bounded by the rollout.
